title: Linking the second messenger cyclic di-GMP signaling with the regulatory activity of the small RNA ErsA in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and unzipped the full Europe PMC supplementary package (1.36 MB): it holds only figure images (.webp/.gif) and one 10-page PDF. I extracted all 10 PDF pages as text: 4 supplementary figure legends (bar charts, no underlying numbers), Table S1 (strains and plasmids, text descriptions), Table S2 (~30 oligonucleotide primers), and a reference list. No spreadsheet, CSV or numeric data file of any kind.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The experimental design (reporter fusions, RT-qPCR, Western/Northern blots at three c-di-GMP levels) comes from the methods text. The Data Availability Statement says only 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material' — no repository accession anywhere in the text, and Europe PMC reports hasDbCrossReferences=N and no text-mined accessions.

a1_downloadable.note: The supplement downloads freely (CC-BY), but it is figures plus a PDF of strain and primer lists — no data file.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no column of anything. Every quantitative result (fluorescence, 2^-delta-delta-Ct) exists only as bars in figure images; a label would have to be reconstructed by digitising plots.

a3_inputs_present.note: No feature table. The only sequences present are ~30 PCR primers in Table S2; target 5' untranslated regions are described in prose, not provided as a sequence file.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are stated in figure legends (relative fluorescence units per optical density, 2^-delta-delta-Ct), but only inside images.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The whole study concerns 4 ErsA target genes (algC, mlaA, oprD, fleN) across 3 c-di-GMP backgrounds, i.e. tens of measurements, versus the ~1,500-row minimum.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially small — that is the problem, not an advantage.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Table S1 and S2 contents match what the methods cite; there are no row counts to disagree about.

a8_label_provenance.note: Measurements are genuine wet-lab readouts (reporter fluorescence, RT-qPCR, blots), not another model's output — but they are not machine-readable.

existing_models.name: sRNARFTarget (random-forest bacterial small-RNA target predictor)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported by its authors as matching or beating IntaRNA while ~100x faster, on transcriptome-wide target prediction; split details not checked by me
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Species-specific small RNAs cannot be handled by the comparative-genomics tool CopraRNA, which is why a sequence-only model was built

existing_models.name: sRNAdeep (DistilBERT-based bacterial small-RNA classifier, BMC Genomics 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Authors report better performance than earlier small-RNA prediction tools; I only read the abstract-level summary, not the split

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Not applicable — there is no table to join.

honest_claim_h3: No model can be trained from this paper: its entire quantitative content is a few dozen reporter and RT-qPCR measurements shown as bar charts, so any claim would rest on digitised figures.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a messenger RNA's untranslated region sequence to predict whether a small RNA represses it under high c-di-GMP signalling.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need pairs of (small-RNA sequence, target 5' untranslated region) with a measured repression strength at defined c-di-GMP (cyclic di-GMP, a bacterial signalling molecule) levels. This paper provides 4 such target genes, not thousands.
plain_idea.predict: Fold change in protein output of the target, measured here by green-fluorescent-protein reporter fusions and RT-qPCR (reverse-transcription quantitative PCR) in engineered Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups working on bacterial post-transcriptional regulation would like a predictor of condition-dependent small-RNA repression, but that needs a high-throughput screen, which this paper is not.

ml_idea: None viable from this paper. The conceptually interesting task — predicting which messenger RNAs a small RNA represses and how that changes with second-messenger levels — would need a high-throughput dataset (for example a reporter library or RNA-RNA interactome sequencing such as RIL-seq), which this paper does not produce or deposit.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimate is meaningful: there is no dataset. The supplement is 1.4 MB of images plus a 10-page PDF, which I opened and read in full.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Unzip the supplementary package and list the files — done in one command; it contains zero tabular data files.

verdict_reason: A classic single-mechanism molecular microbiology paper: the supplement holds only figure images, a strain list and a primer list, so there is no label column (A2), no feature table (A3), and only four target genes measured (A5).
